4.2 Illustrative Examples

  • The following are some of the examples of Recursion: 4.2.1 Mathematical Recursion: Factorial The factorial function is the classic introduction to recursion.
  • The factorial of a non-negative integer n (denoted as n!) is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n.
  • Call Stack Visualization When a recursive function is called, each function call is placed on the call stack.
  • Understanding this stack behavior is crucial for analyzing recursive algorithms.

4.3 Analyzing Recursive Algorithms

  • This section illustrates the process of analyzing recursive algorithms by example.
  • Call Stack Visualization When a recursive function is called, each function call is placed on the call stack.
  • Understanding this stack behavior is crucial for analyzing recursive algorithms.
  • If f(n) = O(n^(log_b(a)-ε)) for ε > 0, then T(n) = Θ(n^log_b(a)) 2.

4.4 Recursion Run Amok

  • If empty, return an empty list (base case) 3.
  • Recursively traverse the left subtree and add its values to result 5.
  • Recursively traverse the right subtree and add its values to result 7.
  • Otherwise, create a result list starting with the current node's value 4.

4.5 Further Examples of Recursion

4.6 Designing Recursive Algorithms

  • In this section, the process of designing recursive algorithms shall be discussed: 4.6.1 The Recursive Design Process Step 1: Identify the Base Case(s) Algorithm for Finding Base Cases: 1.
  • Ask the Fundamental Question: "What is the simplest version of this problem that I can solve directly?" 2.
  • Consider Edge Cases: Think about scenarios where: o Input size is 0 or 1 o Range becomes empty or invalid o Target condition is already met 3.
  • Ensure Termination: The base case must guarantee that recursion stops 4.

4.7 Eliminating Tail Recursion

  • Understanding Tail Recursion Tail recursion occurs when the recursive call is the last operation in the function.
  • This is significant because tail-recursive functions can be optimized by compilers to use constant stack space.
